title: Knowledge check: Responsive and Inclusive UI Design

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Responsive and Inclusive UI Design”?
options: Use a placeholder instead of a permanent label in every form.
Use semantic elements, accessible names, visible keyboard focus, clear text errors, and meaningful status announcements.
Use color alone to communicate an error.
Remove focus indication to keep the interface visually simple.
questions.answer_key: Use semantic elements, accessible names, visible keyboard focus, clear text errors, and meaningful status announcements.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Responsive and Inclusive UI Design directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Responsive CSS with Vue components”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Use CSS or Vue transitions to communicate a real state change and respect reduced-motion preferences.
Animation should be the only signal for errors.
Scoped styles automatically affect every unrelated component.
List movement can be animated reliably without stable identity.
questions.answer_key: Use CSS or Vue transitions to communicate a real state change and respect reduced-motion preferences.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Responsive CSS with Vue components”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Responsive and Inclusive UI Design” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
